issues.legal_issue: For the competence requirement under the rule of res judicata, “suit” refers to the entire subsequent suit, not merely the part or issue that was decided earlier.
material_facts: A prior rent-and-ejectment suit was dismissed because a necessary co-lessor had not been joined.
The same claimant later brought a suit involving the same tenant and a related rent-and-ejectment claim, joining the alleged co-lessor as a pro forma defendant.
The earlier court had decided the issue of whether the claimant could sue alone, but it lacked pecuniary jurisdiction to try the later suit as a whole.
issues.conclusion: The later suit was not barred by res judicata because the earlier court was not competent to try the entire later suit.
issues.legal_principle: Section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure requires the court that decided the earlier matter to have been competent to try the subsequent suit, meaning the whole suit rather than only an issue within it. The Court construed “suit” literally, relying on the legislative history of the res judicata provisions in the Codes of 1859, 1877, 1882 and 1908, and on Duchess of Kingston’s case, Misir Raghobardial v. Rajah Sheo Baksh Singh and Gokul Mandar v. Pudmanund Singh. It also referred to Mussamut Edun v. Mussamut Bechun, Ram Dayal v. Jankidas, Shibo Raut v. Baban Raut and Sheikh Maqsood Ali v. H. Hunter.

rule.if: later_suit_follows_final_prior_decision and same_parties_litigated_prior_issue and same_material_issue_reappears and earlier_court_could_not_try_entire_later_suit

predicates.later_suit_follows_final_prior_decision: A party brought a later suit after a court finally decided an earlier suit.
predicates.same_parties_litigated_prior_issue: The same parties litigated the relevant issue in the earlier suit.
predicates.same_material_issue_reappears: The material issue decided in the earlier suit arose again in the later suit.
predicates.earlier_court_could_not_try_entire_later: The court that decided the earlier suit lacked jurisdiction to try the later suit as a whole.

issues.definition: When the same parties bring a later suit in which a finally decided material issue reappears, the later suit is not barred on that basis if the earlier court could not have tried the later suit as a whole.

issues.legal_issue: A rent note that identifies one person as the owner and treats another named person as an elder relative does not make the latter a co-lessor, and a tenant may not deny the title of the person recognized as lessor.
material_facts: The tenant executed a rent note naming the claimant and the claimant’s mother-in-law.
The rent note required rent to be paid against a receipt from the owner, using the singular.
The note described the claimant as the heir and owner of the property and described the other named person as the elder in the family.
The dispute arose in a suit for rent and ejectment, and the tenant relied on the other person’s inclusion in the note to dispute the claimant’s right to sue alone.
issues.conclusion: The rent note was in favour of the claimant alone; the other person’s name was included formally out of respect, and the tenant was precluded from disputing the claimant’s title.
issues.legal_principle: The rent note must be read as a whole and reasonably construed. Its reference to a singular owner and its description of the claimant as heir and owner showed that the other named person was not a co-lessor. Under section 116 of the Evidence Act, the principles of tenant estoppel applied, precluding the tenant from disputing the claimant’s title as lessor in the proceedings.

predicates.tenant_title_dispute_in_rent_or_ejectmen: A tenant disputed a claimant’s title in a suit concerning rent or ejectment.
predicates.rent_note_names_claimant_and_another_per: The tenant executed a rent note naming the claimant and another person.
predicates.rent_receipt_clause_refers_to_one_owner: The rent note directed the tenant to obtain a receipt from an owner referred to in the singular.
predicates.rent_note_identifies_claimant_as_heir_an: The rent note described the claimant as the heir and owner of the property and the other named person as an elder relative.

issues.definition: When a tenant disputes a claimant’s title in a rent or ejectment suit, the tenant cannot deny that title where the rent note names the claimant and another person, refers to a single owner for rent receipts, and identifies the claimant as heir and owner.
